title: Which MHC molecule presents the antigen?
caption: Where the protein comes from decides the route. Proteins made inside any nucleated cell, including viral proteins, are cut up by the proteasome and shown on MHC class I to cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells. Proteins taken in from outside by antigen-presenting cells are broken down in endosomes and shown on MHC class II to helper CD4⁺ T cells.
alt: A flow chart: a protein made inside the cell goes by the proteasome to MHC class I and cytotoxic CD8 T cells; a protein taken in from outside goes by endosomes to MHC class II and helper CD4 T cells.
description: Was the protein made inside the cell, as a viral protein is? If so: the proteasome breaks it into peptides, which enter the ER, load onto MHC class I and are shown to cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells, which kill the infected cell.

If it was taken in from outside, on a professional antigen-presenting cell (dendritic cell, macrophage or B cell): endosomes break it down, the peptides load onto MHC class II and are shown to helper CD4⁺ T cells.

q1.q: Was the protein made inside the cell, as a viral protein is?

m1.outcome: MHC class I: the proteasome makes peptides, which are shown to cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells that kill the infected cell

m2.outcome: MHC class II: endosomes break down the protein, and the peptides are shown to helper CD4⁺ T cells
